label: In re SwervePay Acquisition — 'up to $53.75 million' against a payment-volume baseline that was itself contested
provenance: PUBLIC RECORD. In re SwervePay Acquisition, LLC (Del. Ch., July 31, 2026). Per Holland & Knight's summary of the opinion: sellers received 'approximately $9.9 million in cash and an additional $10 million in rollover equity at closing', with contingent consideration of 'up to $53.75 million tied to the Target's ability to convert the Platform's existing payments volume onto its own systems during the 2021 earnout period', hinging on 'a single, contested metric: the volume of payments actually flowing through the Platform's systems' — represented as $34 billion, actually about $5.2 billion. Award: $75,692,297 on fraud. Other summaries split the contingent consideration into two milestones ($43.75m and $25m) and larger equity figures; the discrepancy is left unresolved here rather than picked, because it does not change the outcome below.

deal.metricName: Net payments revenue from converted payment volume (2021)

settled.note: No earnout was paid. The $75,692,297 award is fraud damages, not an earnout payment.
